challenge.better_approach: The orchestrator's read: budget from a multiple of the seal's recorded duration, with a floor. Measured: a validation records conditions.timeout (the budget) and no duration, so that shape needs a new evidence field across every seal and a reseal to have anything to read, and it still would not honour a budget the chart declared. Considered having verdict.py append --timeout to the instrument string — that rewrites the builder's command, and breaks any instrument that is not a bare `bin/cairn test`. Carrying the exec bound down is the plainest: the chart's number reaches the proof.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That an instrument which runs several proofs is fine with each getting the whole exec bound: no single proof can outlive the envelope anyway, so the envelope stays the true bound. That the env var reaching a nested bwrap'd shell survives the wrap — iso.wrap passes env through (CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID rides it today).
challenge.prior_art: Ticket 8383a32d20c5 (a proof declares its own time limit, PROOF_TIMEOUT_S) — the per-proof override; it stands and still wins. cairn/devices/tester/cli.py:553 sets the 120 default; run_exec (device.py:914) already sets CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID in the child env, the same channel. Nothing carries the exec's bound inward.
challenge.real_collision: None: 8383a32d20c5's precedence (declared beats caller) stands; this only changes what the caller's default is when the caller is an exec envelope. conditions.changed does not compare timeout, so the moved default posts no notice.

answers.falsifier: Red on d0c7d8376: `cairn test --exec 'printenv CAIRN_TESTER_PROOF_BUDGET' --timeout 300` prints nothing, and `cairn test <fixture sleeping 8 s>` under CAIRN_TESTER_PROOF_BUDGET=3 runs green at the 120 s default. Green: the exec prints 300; the fixture run reports the 3 s budget exceeded; an explicit --timeout, and a proof's PROOF_TIMEOUT_S, each beat the env bound.

answers.how: run_exec exports its bound into the command's env as CAIRN_TESTER_PROOF_BUDGET; the cli's per-proof default reads it (a positive integer) before falling back to 120. An explicit --timeout and a proof's PROOF_TIMEOUT_S still win. Red-first proof in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/.
answers.traces_to: Law 9 / Law 8 — a red must measure distance from the spec; a timeout that measures the box's load is a fake red, and the chart's declared timeout_s (300) was silently replaced by the tester's default (120). Law 7: the declared bound is read, not dropped.
answers.what: A proof run inside `cairn test --exec` with no --timeout of its own and no PROOF_TIMEOUT_S runs at the exec's bound, so the budget a chart declares for an instrument is the budget its proof gets.
